A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RNE/RNC framework and retain matching methods and experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original density-estimation, molecular annealing, multi-target ligand-design and reward-tilting experiments.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices F and I report retained control experiments and new particle-scaling, energy-learning and solvation free-energy results.

M1.justification: v4 adds energy-based diffusion training: scalar energy parametrization and a stop-gradient RNE consistency loss augment denoising score matching (Section 2.2). Appendices I.3–I.4 provide reference-based and stochastic-interpolant implementations. This introduces a substantial training component beyond v1's estimation and inference-time control procedures.

E1.justification: v4 adds energy-learning evaluations on 2D and 100D Gaussian mixtures, MCMC sampling from learned ALDP energies, and free-energy estimation between vacuum and implicit-solvent ALDP. Earlier 10D mixture, annealing and ligand-design coverage remains represented, including reward-tilting plots in Appendix F.4.

E2.justification: New comparisons evaluate standard DSM, Dual SM (Guth et al., 2025; Figure 5), and neural thermodynamic integration without RNE regularization (Table 4). Existing density-estimation comparators and FKC remain. RNC-TDS disappears from the multi-target SBDD comparison but remains in the annealing table.

E3.justification: Original annealing and multi-target SBDD settings are largely retained. Added protocols include a 100–5,000-particle scaling sweep, MCMC-versus-denoising evaluation, and learned-energy correlation measurements. Appendix I.4 specifies 40,000 training iterations and thermodynamic integration using 5,000 samples over 1,000 time steps.

E4.justification: v4 adds particle-count sensitivity analysis, comparisons with and without energy regularization, and checks of learned endpoint energies (Figures 3–6 and 15; Table 2). These examine scaling, energy accuracy and effects on diffusion sample quality. Earlier reference-process and ESS analyses remain; v1's illustrated ligand examples are removed.

E5.justification: Appendix I.4 explicitly reports three repetitions of the new thermodynamic-integration experiments and summarizes their means and standard deviations. v1 already used ± reporting in molecular-result tables. This adds a statistical reporting protocol for a new experiment without establishing additional runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: New results include ALDP MCMC W2 of 0.1836 with RNE versus 0.9472 with DSM, and TI estimates of 29.28±0.04 with RNE versus 27.30±0.45 without it, against a 29.43±0.01 reference. Original annealing and shared SBDD values are unchanged. The SBDD RNC-TDS row and v1's aggregate reward-tilting Table 3 are removed, while pocket-level reward plots remain.

T1.justification: v4 Appendix C.5 explicitly retracts v1's exact-weight argument for imperfect-model annealing/product because the omitted normalization depends on the endpoint; exact cancellation is restricted to reward tilting. v4 also adds derivations connecting energy regularization to the Fokker–Planck equation and recovering a second, Laplacian-free reward-FKC formulation. Existing convergence and CTMC derivations largely survive relocation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion expand the central contribution to energy-based diffusion training and introduce a claim of favorable inference-time scaling. The unification claim now includes Fokker–Planck regularization. Density estimation and inference-time control remain contributions, although density estimation receives less main-text emphasis.

C2.justification: v1 treated imperfect-model cancellation weights as exact and explained weaker performance through ESS. v4 instead explains the normalization obstruction and explicitly acknowledges biased annealing/composition in Appendix B. It also adds interpretations of score-matching blindness, energy accuracy versus diffusion sample quality, and TI errors caused by mismatch between interpolant samples and learned energies.

D1.justification: v4 adds RNC pseudocode, energy-network and Dual SM implementation details, regularization settings of 1000 and a time increment of 0.0001, and extensive stochastic-interpolant/TI training and estimation instructions. Earlier annealing and multi-target SBDD details largely remain. However, v1 Appendix D.3's controllable-SBDD implementation details disappear despite retained reward-tilting plots.

R1.justification: Positioning expands substantially toward energy-based diffusion, force fields and free-energy estimation, including Guth, Máté and Plainer. New Appendix J distinguishes RNE from RND-based samplers with tractable intermediate densities. Appendix C.1 newly acknowledges Skreta's earlier discrete Gaussian estimator, while Appendix H.4.4 recognizes a newer Laplacian-free FKC formulation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are rewritten around control and energy-based training. Existing density-estimation and importance-sampling sections move into Appendix C, the experimental narrative is condensed, and limitations, connections and implementation guidance receive reorganized appendix sections. This substantially changes the narrative and document structure beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: v4 adds scaling, learned-density, energy-correlation and Ramachandran plots, two result tables and a pseudocode figure. The method-connection diagram is redrawn and expanded, and existing density-estimation plots move into the appendix. v1's ligand-example figure and reward-tilting table are removed; the main experimental page uses a substantially rearranged, denser layout.

improvement.justification: The explicit normalization erratum corrects a consequential false guarantee in v1 and clarifies the method's actual applicability. v4 also documents and evaluates a substantial energy-training extension through DSM/Dual SM comparisons, sampling checks and repeated free-energy estimates. Removing the aggregate reward-tilting results and settings weakens documentation, and the surviving RNC-TDS annealing row is unexplained. These gaps do not outweigh the important correction and added validation.
